name: Rapid Search
summary: Shopify app that replaces the search icon with an always-visible AI search bar (typo tolerance, synonyms, instant results, SKU search) and adds product and collection filters on tags and metafields, hand-set pins and boosts, and search analytics.
best_for: Shopify stores whose shoppers arrive knowing what they want, with catalogues from a few hundred to 100,000 products, that want typo-tolerant instant search, filters on tags and metafields and hand-set pins and boosts without editing theme code
skip_if: you sell outside Shopify; your catalogue is past 100,000 products, which only the $349 unlimited tier covers; or you have heavy traffic and light search use, because the meter counts every visit, not every search
honest_knock:
The meter is your traffic, not your searches. Rapid Search prices on monthly sessions, and its own FAQ defines a session as a visit to the store. A shopper who never touches the search box still counts. So the plan you need follows your total storefront traffic: 2,000 sessions free, 5,000 on the $14 tier, 25,000 on the $39 tier. A store with modest search use but a lot of visitors pays for headroom it does not search with.

Going over the cap does not bill you, it switches you back. The vendor's FAQ says it sends several warnings as you approach the limit, and that if you do not upgrade, search reverts to Shopify's built-in search until the limit resets with the next charge. That is more honest than a surprise overage, but it means the best month of the year is the month your search can quietly downgrade itself. Upgrade before a sale, not during it.

The two pricing pages tell different stories. The Shopify listing stops at Basic 3, $39 a month for 25,000 sessions. The vendor's pricing slider goes on to $59, $79, $129, $199 and $349 a month, and the product cap stays at 100,000 on every tier up to $199; the listing's line that it scales to 1M+ products describes only the $349 unlimited tier. The customer logos (Levi's, Skechers, alo) and the claims of 5,000+ stores and a doubled search conversion rate come from the vendor's own site and are not sourced there. We installed it in a Shopify development store on 16 Nov 2026.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic 1 · per month for 5,000 monthly sessions and 100,000 products, unbranded, billed through Shopify every 30 days with a 14-day free trial
pricing.notes: (read 26 Sep 2026 and 21 Oct 2026; the Shopify listing was read again on 16 Nov 2026, the vendor's own pricing page was last read on 21 Oct 2026) Every plan carries every feature; the tiers differ only in monthly sessions and catalogue size. The Shopify listing shows four tiers. Free covers 2,000 monthly sessions and 1,000 products with email support (the listing said 5,000 products when we read it on 21 Oct 2026), and the search carries Rapid Search branding. Basic 1 is $14 a month, or $140 a year, for 5,000 sessions and 100,000 products; Basic 2 is $27 a month, or $270 a year, for 12,000 sessions; Basic 3 is $39 a month, or $390 a year, for 25,000 sessions. The paid tiers are unbranded, add chat support and start with a 14 day free trial (listing, read 16 Nov 2026). The listing also says paid plans have 30% off applied after install, without a term or amounts. In the app on 16 Nov 2026 a 30% discount on the first 3 months was shown: Basic 1 $10 then $14, Basic 2 $19 then $27, Basic 3 $27 then $39, and the 45,000 session tier $41 then $59. In the app, new installs also got a trial with unlimited sessions; the listing does not mention that. The vendor's pricing slider continues past the listing: $59 a month for 45,000 sessions, $79 for 75,000, $129 for 130,000 and $199 for 500,000, all still capped at 100,000 products, and $349 a month for unlimited sessions and 1,000,000 products. The listing quotes annual billing as a 17% saving and only for the three Basic tiers. The vendor site says the trial needs no credit card and offers a refund within the first 30 days on a paid plan. All charges are in USD through Shopify's billing, every 30 days.

compare_with.name: Dynasort
compare_with.why: Dynasort is the closest comparison in our own dossiers, and it does a different job on the same catalogue. Dynasort (read 15 September 2026) re-orders your collection pages automatically from sales, stock and margin signals, starting at $99 a month for 25 sorted collections after a free demo tier. Rapid Search makes the search box and the filters work: typo tolerance, synonyms, instant results, filters on price, tags and metafields, and merchandising you set by hand, pinning, boosting, demoting or hiding products in the results. Its paid tiers start at $14 a month and are sized on store sessions rather than collections. A store that loses shoppers at the search box starts here; a store that loses them scrolling a badly ordered collection starts with Dynasort. The two do not replace each other.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Rapid Search on a Shopify development store inside a free trial: the onboarding, a search with a typing error, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid or uninstalled. In the theme editor App embeds list, Rapid Search App was already switched on by the app (Save greyed out) and Rapid Search CSB was off; no theme change was saved. The search icon in the preview opens an overlay with popular searches and popular products. Typing snowbord (a typing error for snowboard) at about 14:34:30 showed, within about 2 seconds, PRODUCTS with The Complete Snowboard $699.95 In stock, The Videographer Snowboard $885.95, The Collection Snowboard: Liquid $749.95, The Collection Snowboard: Oxygen $1,025.00 and The Multi-managed Snowboard $629.95, the suggestions snowboard and collection snowboard, the button View all snowbord products and powered by: Rapid Search. View all opened a results page that the app had created, with 13 results for snowbord, filters Category (Automated Collection 6, Hydrogen 3) and Product Type (snowboard 12, giftcard 1), a price slider from $10 to $2630 and sorting by Relevance. Timing, approximate tester observations: Install at 14:30:26 and the right results at 14:34:30, about 4 minutes, mostly our own clicks and the refused first email; the store data synchronisation finished within about 20 seconds (Downloading data, Processing data, Synchronization finished) and the results appeared within about 2 seconds of typing; about 12 steps in all. Settings, Apps shows a menu for the app with Open app, View details, Get support and Uninstall; the Uninstall dialog was opened and cancelled. Not tested: a paid plan, the yearly plan after approval, the 75K to Unlimited prices, collection pages and filters, product merchandising, Statistics, real traffic counting sessions and what happens after 30 Nov. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The onboarding asks for a reachable email address before the app works, and a made up example address was refused.

findings: Vendor claim "5,000 products". What we saw: The dossier named 5,000 products on the Free plan. The Free plan in the app shows Up to 1.000 products; the 2K session limit matched. The Free plan covers up to 1.000 products, so a store with more products needs a paid plan sooner than the dossier suggested.

Vendor claim "installs in one click, no code, live within minutes". What we saw: Installing took one click and no code. Before the search worked the app asked for 3 onboarding screens and a reachable email address; a made up example address was refused. Search results appeared about 4 minutes after Install, in about 12 steps. The one click install holds, but a reachable email address and 3 onboarding screens come first.

Vendor claim "14-day free trial on paid tiers". What we saw: Shopify showed a 14-day free trial ending on 30 Nov for the 5K plan. The app also gives every store unlimited sessions and products until November 30, 2026 without choosing a plan, after which the Free limits apply. The trial exists on the paid plan and runs to 30 Nov; afterwards the Free limits apply if no plan is chosen.

Vendor claim "Unbranded". What we saw: The 5K plan lists Unbranded and the Free plan lists Branded; the overlay on the trial showed powered by: Rapid Search. Whether the branding disappears on a paid plan was not tested. Free search carries the Rapid Search branding; removing it needs a paid plan.

Vendor claim "First 3 months, then $14/month". What we saw: The 5K plan card shows $10/month with $14 struck through, First 3 months, then $14/month. The Shopify Approve subscription screen for Rapid Search Basic 1 Plan showed Subtotal $14,00, Discount -$4,00 and Total $10,00 due 30 Nov after a 14-day free trial, plus any applicable taxes. Card and approval screen agree on 10 and 14 dollars; tax is unknown and nothing was approved. About $10 for each of the first 3 months after the trial and then $14, before any taxes.
